guard: bare cotal, help and version read local metadata only and every usage error is refused before any effect: an unknown command, a prefix, an unknown flag, a missing value or an undeclared subcommand writes no seed store, while a valid command does; an alias resolves as its command does in help, refusal and parse, and a subcommand alias reaches the command as its canonical word
command: pnpm --filter cotal-ai... build && pnpm exec tsx bin/smoke/cli-entry.smoke.ts
why: The connector seed ran before the command was resolved or its flags parsed, so a mistyped flag installed the built-in connectors and only then printed the refusal. Each mutation restores one way the front end can stop being local or stop resolving aliases canonically, and must redden the cell that names it. The suite drives the built binary, so each mutation rebuilds and the restore rebuilds back.

mutations.name: the seed runs before flag parsing
mutations.find: let parsed = cmd && !isExtensionStub(cmd) ? parseOrExit(cmd, rest) : undefined;
mutations.replace:
if (opts.extensions && !skipsSeed(cmd?.name ?? word, rest[0], rest)) await reconcileSeededConnectors();
  let parsed = cmd && !isExtensionStub(cmd) ? parseOrExit(cmd, rest) : undefined;
mutations.expectRed: an unknown flag writes no seed store
mutations.cell: an unknown flag writes no seed store
mutations.command: pnpm --filter cotal-ai... build && pnpm exec tsx bin/smoke/cli-entry.smoke.ts
mutations.note: The defect this change fixes: a resolved command seeded before its flags were parsed, so a usage error installed the connectors first. Restoring the whole pre-split order makes nearly every invocation in the suite seed and outruns the proof's per-run budget.
